paragraphs.source_en: For some time now, I hear, Japan has been waging a great war against Russia. As I am a Japanese cat, naturally I favor Japan. I have even thought that, if possible, I should like to organize a mixed brigade of cats and scratch those Russian soldiers with our claws. With such valor and vigor as mine, if only I chose to do it, catching one or two mice would of course be nothing at all. Long ago, someone asked a famous Zen master of the day, “How may one attain complete enlightenment?” The Zen master is said to have replied, “Be as a cat is when it fixes its eye upon a mouse.” In saying that one should be like a cat catching a mouse, he meant that, so long as one does so, one cannot miss the mark. There is a proverb about women being over-clever, but I have never heard any maxim saying, “A cat, through being too clever, fails to catch mice.” That being so, no matter how clever I may be, there can be no reason why I should be unable to catch mice. The only reason I have not caught mice until now is simply that I did not care to catch them. As on the day before, the spring day passed into evening; now and then a gust of wind sent a snowstorm of falling blossoms dancing in through a tear in the kitchen’s low sliding screen, and the petals reflected on the water in the bucket looked white in the dim lamplight of the kitchen. I then resolved that tonight I would achieve some distinguished feat and make the whole household look at me with new respect. First, I had to reconnoiter the terrain of the battlefield. The battle line, of course, was hardly extensive; measured in tatami mats, it was no more than four and a half mats. Of that, a space of about one mat was divided so that half was the sink and half was an earthen floor where the vegetable seller’s errand boy could come in and stand. The cooking range, for its part, was splendid, quite out of keeping with our poor kitchen, and the red copper kettle on it shone brightly. Behind it, in a two-foot space left between it and the wooden wall, there lay an abalone shell; that was my dining place. Along the six-foot stretch next to the living room stood a cupboard containing bowls, plates, basins, jars, and the like. It partitioned off the already narrow kitchen and made it narrower still. The cupboard was nearly the same height as the horizontal open shelf and pressed close up against it. Beneath the shelf a mortar was set upside down, and inside the mortar the bottom of a small tub faced toward me. A pestle and a daikon grater hung on the wall, and beside them a fire-extinguishing pot stood quietly by. From the crossed beams, blackened with soot, a hook hung down, and at its end was suspended a large basket. This basket swayed now and then in the wind, swinging left and right with an air of importance. When I first came to this house I could not for the life of me understand why they hung that basket there; only later did I learn that they deliberately put food in it and hung it up so that we cats could not get our paws on it. That made me feel, with painful clarity, just how spiteful human beings truly are.

units.source_en: For some time now, I hear, Japan has been waging a great war against Russia.

units.source_zh: 前一阵子，听说日本和俄罗斯展开了大战。

units.source_zh: 据说那位禅师回答说，“应当像猫儿瞄准老鼠那样。”

units.source_zh: 俗语中有女人好耍小聪明的说法，可还没有听说过这样的格言：“猫儿因好耍小聪明而捉不住老鼠。”

units.source_en: That being so, no matter how clever I may be, there can be no reason why I should be unable to catch mice.
units.source_zh: 这样看来，不管我如何耍小聪明，总不至于捉不住老鼠的。

units.source_zh: 过去我之所以没有捉老鼠，只不过是我不想捉它而已。

units.source_zh: 春日一如昨天那样，又到了黄昏时刻，一阵风过，落花如雪，从厨房隔扇的破洞里飞舞进来，花瓣儿映在水桶的水面上，在昏暗的厨房灯光下显得白花花的。

units.source_en: I then resolved that tonight I would achieve some distinguished feat and make the whole household look at me with new respect.
units.source_zh: 我这时下定决心，一定要在今夜建立个殊勋，使全家人都对我刮目相看。

units.source_en: First, I had to reconnoiter the terrain of the battlefield.
units.source_zh: 首先，我必须侦察好战场的地形。

units.source_zh: 当然战线并不太广阔，用叠数来估量也不过是四叠半那么大。

units.source_en: Of that, a space of about one mat was divided so that half was the sink and half was an earthen floor where the vegetable seller’s errand boy could come in and stand.
units.source_zh: 其中有一叠大小的地方，一半是洗菜池，一半是泥土地面，那是供菜铺子小伙计进来站脚的地方。

units.source_en: The cooking range, for its part, was splendid, quite out of keeping with our poor kitchen, and the red copper kettle on it shone brightly.
units.source_zh: 炉灶嘛，和我家的穷厨房不相称，很气派，上边的赤铜壶也精光锃亮。

units.source_en: Behind it, in a two-foot space left between it and the wooden wall, there lay an abalone shell; that was my dining place.
units.source_zh: 在它的后面，和木板壁之间留有两尺的地方，放有一个鲍鱼壳，是我进餐的地方。

units.source_en: Along the six-foot stretch next to the living room stood a cupboard containing bowls, plates, basins, jars, and the like.
units.source_zh: 和起居间相邻的六尺地方放有柜橱，装着碗、碟、盆、罐之类。

units.source_en: It partitioned off the already narrow kitchen and made it narrower still.
units.source_zh: 把本来狭小的厨房割得更加狭窄。

units.source_en: The cupboard was nearly the same height as the horizontal open shelf and pressed close up against it.
units.source_zh: 柜橱的高度和横架着的壁橱相差无几，紧紧贴近着。

units.source_en: Beneath the shelf a mortar was set upside down, and inside the mortar the bottom of a small tub faced toward me.
units.source_zh: 壁橱的下边一只捣罐仰放着，捣罐中的小桶的桶底对着我。

units.source_en: A pestle and a daikon grater hung on the wall, and beside them a fire-extinguishing pot stood quietly by.
units.source_zh: 在墙上挂着的捣槌和萝卜礤子，旁边悄然地立着一只消火罐。

units.source_en: From the crossed beams, blackened with soot, a hook hung down, and at its end was suspended a large basket.
units.source_zh: 从变得黢黑的房椽子交叉的地方垂下来的一根吊钩，在它的顶端挂着一只大篮子。

units.source_en: This basket swayed now and then in the wind, swinging left and right with an air of importance.
units.source_zh: 这只篮子不时在风中摇晃，大模大样地左右摆动。

units.source_en: When I first came to this house I could not for the life of me understand why they hung that basket there; only later did I learn that they deliberately put food in it and hung it up so that we cats could not get our paws on it.
units.source_zh: 为什么要将这只篮子挂在那里，我初来这家时简直弄不明白，后来才知道他们是为了不让我们猫儿染指，才故意把食物放在篮子里边吊起来。

units.source_zh: 这使我深深地体会到人的心眼儿真是坏透了。

paragraphs.source_zh: 前一阵子，听说日本和俄罗斯展开了大战。我是只日本猫儿，当然是偏向日本。我甚至想：“如果可能，组织个猫儿混成旅用爪子去挠挠那些俄国兵呢。”从我这种勇猛的劲儿来说，只要我愿意，去捉上一两只老鼠，当然不在话下。古时候，有人问当时一位有名的禅师：“怎样才能大彻大悟？”据说那位禅师回答说，“应当像猫儿瞄准老鼠那样。”他之所以说应该像猫捉鼠，其意思就是说如果那样就不会无的放矢。俗语中有女人好耍小聪明的说法，可还没有听说过这样的格言：“猫儿因好耍小聪明而捉不住老鼠。”这样看来，不管我如何耍小聪明，总不至于捉不住老鼠的。过去我之所以没有捉老鼠，只不过是我不想捉它而已。春日一如昨天那样，又到了黄昏时刻，一阵风过，落花如雪，从厨房隔扇的破洞里飞舞进来，花瓣儿映在水桶的水面上，在昏暗的厨房灯光下显得白花花的。我这时下定决心，一定要在今夜建立个殊勋，使全家人都对我刮目相看。首先，我必须侦察好战场的地形。当然战线并不太广阔，用叠数来估量也不过是四叠半那么大。其中有一叠大小的地方，一半是洗菜池，一半是泥土地面，那是供菜铺子小伙计进来站脚的地方。炉灶嘛，和我家的穷厨房不相称，很气派，上边的赤铜壶也精光锃亮。在它的后面，和木板壁之间留有两尺的地方，放有一个鲍鱼壳，是我进餐的地方。和起居间相邻的六尺地方放有柜橱，装着碗、碟、盆、罐之类。把本来狭小的厨房割得更加狭窄。柜橱的高度和横架着的壁橱相差无几，紧紧贴近着。壁橱的下边一只捣罐仰放着，捣罐中的小桶的桶底对着我。在墙上挂着的捣槌和萝卜礤子，旁边悄然地立着一只消火罐。从变得黢黑的房椽子交叉的地方垂下来的一根吊钩，在它的顶端挂着一只大篮子。这只篮子不时在风中摇晃，大模大样地左右摆动。为什么要将这只篮子挂在那里，我初来这家时简直弄不明白，后来才知道他们是为了不让我们猫儿染指，才故意把食物放在篮子里边吊起来。这使我深深地体会到人的心眼儿真是坏透了。
